rachel: Rolling lexicon-lite-v0 into staging for embeddings bring-up. Quick sanity pass shows odd drop in recall@10 after block-quant int4 (block size=32). Posting numbers + what I ran.

rachel: Baseline fp16 recall@10 (enwiki-1k): 0.912
int8 (symmetric) recall@10: 0.908 (-0.4)
int4 block32 recall@10: 0.873 (-3.9)
int4 block16 recall@10: 0.884 (-2.8)
silhouette (kmeans=200) fp16: 0.42; int4 block32: 0.35 -> clusters smear.

kevin: Interesting that block16 helps vs block32. Can you paste the exact eval command and the quant pipeline?

rachel: Eval command and quant steps: ```bash
# eval
python harness/emb_eval.py --model lexicon-lite --weights /models/lexicon-lite/int4-block32.pth --holdout s3://redwood-evals/enwiki_holdout/1k.jsonl --k 10 --sim cosine --whiten none --normalize true --batch 256

# quant pipeline (offline):
python quant/quantize.py --model /checkpoints/lexicon-lite/fp16.ckpt --mode block --bits 4 --block-size 32 --calib s3://redwood-evals/anchors/5k.jsonl --method lsq
```

izzy: Are you using LSQ with per-channel scales inside each block or per-block single scale? That changes effective dynamic range. Also did you fold layernorm/bias before quant?

rachel: Using LSQ with per-channel (within block) scales. We folded LayerNorm where possible, but bias terms kept. I didn't fold residual add (can't easily).

noah: How are you computing nearest neighbors? Approx or exact? ANN can change recall numbers slightly.

rachel: Exact brute-force dot with faiss CPU index for these runs. Also checked top-1 labeling; some topical anchors jump to other centroids post-quant.

kevin: Two quick experiments to try: 1) calibrate per-dim bias using 10k anchors and then apply small per-dim scaling clamp (0.98-1.02). 2) Try block32 but with mixed-precision: first and last transformer blocks kept at int8/fp16, middle blocks int4. Could preserve high-level semantics.

izzy: Also try whitening (PCA128) vs no-whiten. Whitening sometimes amplifies small quant errors but can help directional noise. And compute cosine vs l2 to sanity check.

rachel: Good call. I'll queue: run_a = int4-block32+10k-calib, run_b = int4-block32-mixed(last/first fp16), run_c = int4-block16 (current). Storing configs at s3://redwood-dev/lexicon-lite/onboard/configs/1777001234/

eval-bot: Jobs created: run_a=1777001234-a, run_b=1777001234-b, run_c=1777001234-c. Started 1777001400. ETA ~30m. Will post recall/k-curves + kmeans UMAP snapshots.

noah: Add a short-query split (<=8 tokens) and a single-token set. Also add a 'rare-token' cohort (queries with <5 occurrences in wiki) to see fragility.

rachel: Added cohorts. Also adding synthetic perturbation test: multiplicative noise per-dim (1 +/- 0.01) and additive gaussian sigma=0.01. If int4 causes higher sensitivity we'll see recall slope.

kevin: If mixed-precision recovers ~2% without cost blowup we can propose a hybrid profile for Dedicated customers. Otherwise fallback to int8 for critical routes.

izzy: FYI: if we plan to ship int4, update the rollout plan to include canary on non-short queries and auto-fallback for flagged cohorts. I can draft rollout policy.

rachel: Thanks all. Will post results when eval-bot reports back. :rocket:
